sections.en: If five men filled five jars to prepare with them five mixtures, and then they changed their minds to prepare one mixture from all of them, or if they filled the jars to prepare with them one mixture and then they changed their minds to prepare with them five mixtures, all the water remains valid. If one man filled five jars intending to prepare five [separate] mixtures, [even though] he changed his mind to prepare one mixture from all of them, only the last is valid. If he intended to prepare one mixture from all of them and then he changed his mind to prepare five separate mixtures, only the water in the one that was mixed first is valid. If he said to another man, "Prepare mixtures from these for yourself," only the first is valid; But if he said, "Prepare a mixture from these for me," all are valid.
sections.he: חֲמִשָּׁה שֶׁמִּלְאוּ חֲמִשָּׁה חָבִיּוֹת לְקַדְּשָׁן חֲמִשָּׁה קִדּוּשִׁין, וְנִמְלְכוּ לְקַדְּשָׁן קִדּוּשׁ אֶחָד, אוֹ לְקַדְּשָׁן קִדּוּשׁ אֶחָד וְנִמְלְכוּ לְקַדְּשָׁן חֲמִשָּׁה קִדּוּשִׁין, הֲרֵי כֻלָּן כְּשֵׁרִים. יָחִיד שֶׁמִּלֵּא חָמֵשׁ חָבִיּוֹת לְקַדְּשָׁן חֲמִשָּׁה קִדּוּשִׁין, וְנִמְלַךְ לְקַדְּשָׁן קִדּוּשׁ אֶחָד, אֵין כָּשֵׁר אֶלָּא אַחֲרוֹן. לְקַדְּשָׁן קִדּוּשׁ אֶחָד וְנִמְלַךְ לְקַדְּשָׁן חֲמִשָּׁה קִדּוּשִׁין, אֵין כָּשֵׁר אֶלָּא זֶה שֶׁקִּדֵּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן. אָמַר לְאֶחָד, קַדֵּשׁ לְךָ אֶת אֵלּוּ, אֵין כָּשֵׁר אֶלָּא רִאשׁוֹן. קַדֵּשׁ לִי אֶת אֵלּוּ, הֲרֵי כֻלָּם כְּשֵׁרִים:

comments.en: מִילּוּי, מִלּ׳ m. (מָלֵא) filling, drawing water. Parah VII, 2 המלאכה פוסלת במ׳ labor during the act of filling makes the water unfit (for the sprinkling ceremony). Tosefta ib. IV (III), 11. Yerushalmi Sukkah IV, 54ᶜ bottom of page צריך שיהא מִילּוּיָין לשם החג the water must be drawn especially for the purpose of libation on the Festival. Bavli Sukkah 54ᵃ אין תוקעין למ׳ המים וכ׳ on the Sabbath (during the festival of Succoth) the horn is not blown at drawing water for the altar; and e.—V. מִלּוּא.

sections.en: One who filled the water with one hand and did some other work with the other hand, or filled the water for himself and for another man, or filled two jars at the same time, the water of both is invalid, for work causes invalidity whether one acts for oneself or for another person.
sections.he: הַמְמַלֵּא בְאַחַת יָדוֹ וְעוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכָה בְאַחַת יָדוֹ, הַמְמַלֵּא לוֹ וּלְאַחֵר, אוֹ שֶׁמִּלֵּא לִשְׁנַיִם כְּאַחַת, שְׁנֵיהֶן פְּסוּלִין, שֶׁהַמְּלָאכָה פוֹסֶלֶת בַּמִּלּוּי, בֵּין לוֹ בֵּין לְאַחֵר:

sections.en: One who prepared the mixture with one hand and did some other work with the other hand, the mixture is invalid if he prepared it for himself, but if he prepared it for another man, it is valid. If he prepared a mixture both for himself and for another man, his is invalid and that of the other man is valid. If he prepares mixtures for two men simultaneously, both are valid.
sections.he: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ בְּאַחַת יָדוֹ וְעוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכָה בְאַחַת יָדוֹ, אִם לוֹ, פָּסוּל. וְאִם לְאַחֵר, כָּשֵׁר. הַמְקַדֵּשׁ לוֹ וּלְאַחֵר, שֶׁלּוֹ פָּסוּל, וְשֶׁל אַחֵר כָּשֵׁר. הַמְקַדֵּשׁ לִשְׁנַיִם כְּאֶחָד, שְׁנֵיהֶן כְּשֵׁרִין:

sections.en: [If one said to another] "Prepare the mixture for me and I will prepare the one for you," the first is valid. [If he said,] "Fill the water for me and I will fill the water for you," that of the latter is valid. [If he said,] "Prepare the mixture for me and I will draw the water for you," both mixtures are valid. [If he said,] "Fill the water for me and I will prepare the mixture for you’, both mixtures are invalid.
sections.he: קַדֵּשׁ לִי וַאֲקַדֵּשׁ לָךְ, הָרִאשׁוֹן כָּשֵׁר. מַלֵּא לִי וַאֲמַלֵּא לָךְ, הָאַחֲרוֹן כָּשֵׁר. קַדֵּשׁ לִי וַאֲמַלֵּא לָךְ, שְׁנֵיהֶם כְּשֵׁרִים. מַלֵּא לִי וַאֲקַדֵּשׁ לָךְ, שְׁנֵיהֶם פְּסוּלִים:

comments.en: אָסֵל, אָסֵיל m. (סלל; compare Gr. ἄσιλλα) a pole or yoke carried on two or, more commonly, on one shoulder. Parah VII, 5 וקושרו בא׳ and fastens the bucket to the pole. Kelim XVII, 16 הא׳ שיש בו וכ׳ a carrying yoke in which there is a (hidden) receptacle for money; Kohelet Rabbah to IX, 13 אסיל.

sections.en: One who is drawing water for his own use and for the mixture of the hatat, he must draw for himself first and fasten [the bucket] to the carrying pole and then he can draw the water for the hatat. If he drew first the water for the hatat and then he drew the water for himself, it is invalid. He must put his own behind him and that for the hatat before him, and if he put that for the hatat behind him it is invalid. If both were for the hatat, he may put one before him and one behind him and both are valid, since it is impossible to do otherwise.
sections.he: הַמְמַלֵּא לוֹ וּלְחַטָּאת, מְמַלֵּא אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ תְּחִלָּה וְקוֹשְׁרוֹ בָאֵסֶל וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְמַלֵּא אֶת שֶׁל חַטָּאת. וְאִם מִלֵּא שֶׁל חַטָּאת תְּחִלָּה וְאַחַר כָּךְ מִלֵּא אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ, פָּסוּל. נוֹתֵן אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ לַאֲחוֹרָיו וְאֶת שֶׁל חַטָּאת לְפָנָיו. וְאִם נָתַן אֶת שֶׁל חַטָּאת לַאֲחוֹרָיו, פָּסוּל. הָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶן שֶׁל חַטָּאת, נוֹתֵן אֶחָד לְפָנָיו וְאֶחָד לַאֲחוֹרָיו, וְכָשֵׁר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר:

sections.en: One who carries the rope in his hand, If in his usual manner, the mixture is valid; But if not in his usual manner, it is invalid. The question was sent on to Yavneh on three festivals and on the third festival, it was ruled that the mixture was valid, as a temporary measure.
sections.he: הַמּוֹלִיךְ אֶת הַחֶבֶל בְּיָדוֹ לְדַרְכּוֹ, כָּשֵׁר. וְשֶׁלֹּא לְדַרְכּוֹ, פָּסוּל. זֶה הָלַךְ לְיַבְנֶה שְׁלשָׁה מוֹעֲדוֹת, וּבְמוֹעֵד שְׁלִישִׁי הִכְשִׁירוּ לוֹ הוֹרָאַת שָׁעָה:

comments.en:
כָּנַן (compare כּוּן and כּוֹנָנִית) to nest.—Denom. כִּינָּה.

    Piël - כִּנֵּן to form circles, to wind around. Parah VII, 7 המְכַנֵּן … על יד על יד (Talmud ed. only once על יד) he who winds the rope (for drawing the bucket up) around his hand until a sufficient length is wound up; ואם כִּנְּנוֹ באחרונה but if he winds it after he has finished drawing; Tosefta ib. VII (VI), 4 וחזר ובנאו ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant וכי, read: וכיננו as Rabbenu Shimshon to Parah l. common gender.).—Part. pass. מְכוּנָּן a) wound around. Makhshirin IV, 1 בחבל שהוא מכ׳ וכ׳
with the rope which is wound around the neck of the vessel.—2) nested. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 37 מכ׳ כביצה shut up in the nest like an egg, i.e. selfish; Yalkut Psalms 832 מכונה (correct accordingly).

sections.en: If a man coils the rope around his hand little by little, [the mixture] is valid; But if he coiled it afterwards, it is invalid. Rabbi Yose said: this also had been ruled to be valid as a temporary measure.
sections.he: הַמְכַנֵּן אֶת הַחֶבֶל עַל יָד עַל יָד, כָּשֵׁר. וְאִם כִּנְּנוֹ בָאַחֲרוֹנָה, פָּסוּל. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, לָזֶה הִכְשִׁירוּ הוֹרָאַת שָׁעָה:

comments.en:
חָזַק (Biblical Hebrew; compare אדק, הדק, חדק) [to squeeze together,] (neut. verb) to be thick, solid; to be strong. Yerushalmi Berakhot I, 2ᶜ bottom of page (reference. to Breishit I, 6) יֶחֱזַק הרקיע וכ׳ let the expanse become solidified, let it coagulate, congeal; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 4; (Yalkut ib. 5 יתחזק, Hithpaël).

    Piël - חִיזֵּק to join, repair, tighten, strengthen. Sanhedrin 94ᵃ (explained חזקיה) שחי׳ את ישראל וכ׳ (Manuscript Munich שהחזיק, Hifil) he joined Israel to their Father &c. Ib. שחִזְּקוֹ יה the Lord strengthened him. Pesachim 45ᵃ שעשוי לחַזֵּק Manuscript Munich where the dough in the cracks is put in for repairing the trough. Shabbat 146ᵇ (העשוי) לחַ׳ when the hole was filled up for making the vessel sound, opposed לשמר to prevent evaporation; and from—Part. pass. מְחוּזָּק, plural מְחוּזָּקִים. Sifré Bamidbar 1 אין מְחַזְּקִים אלא המח׳ (ed. תמוחז׳) only the strong-minded it is worth while to strengthen (encourage).

    Hifil - הֶחֱזִיק
1) same, see supra.— same, see supra.—ה׳ טובה ל־ to attach merit to, to account as merit, to be grateful. Pirkei Avot II, 8 אל תַּחֲזִיק ט׳ לעצמך do not claim credit for it (be not proud). Yoma 86ᵇ אלא שמַחֲזִיק לו ט׳ but He even gives him credit (for his sins when he repents). Menachot 53ᵃ הַחֲזֵק לי וכ׳ give me credit for making Thee known &c. Ketubot 68ᵃ, and e. בואו ונַחֲזִיק וכ׳ let us be thankful to the fraudulent poor &c.; and from

—2) (with יד) to strengthen, to encourage, abet. Gittin V, 9 לפי שאין מַחֲזִיקִין וכ׳ because we must not encourage (by favors) those who do wrong. Ib. ומחזיקין ידי עכו"ם וכ׳ we may encourage (greet with תחזקנה ידיכם, Zechariah VIII, 9) gentiles at agricultural work in the Sabbatical year; and from

—3) to hold, contain. Ib. 57ᵃ אין עורו מחזיק וכ׳ its skin (once flayed) can not again cover its entire body (it shrinks). Ib. (in Chald. dict.) אפי׳ שתין … לא מ׳ it would not have room even for sixty myriads of reeds. Parah VII, 8 בשביל שתַּחֲזִיק וכ׳ in order that it (the reservoir) might hold more water. 'Uktzin III, 12 לא מצא … מחזיק וכ׳ the Lord found no vessel so fit to contain all blessings as peace; Devarim Rabbah section (Parashah) 5 end; and from

—4) (with ב) to take a hold of, seize, take possession. Chullin 4ᵃ, and e. כל מצוה שהֶחֱזִיקוּ וכ׳ whatever Jewish law the Samaritans have adopted &c., see דִּקְדֵּק. Bava Metzia I, 4 וה׳ בה and took a hold of it. Bava Batra III, 3 במַחֲזִיק when one is in possession (basing his claim on possession). Ib. המַ׳ בנכסי הגר he who takes possession of the estate of a convert (who has no heirs in law). Ib. 2 ויַחֲזִיק שנה that he may be in possession for one year, see אִסְפַּמְיָא; and from; see חֲזָקָה.—Yerushalmi Chagigah I, 76ᶜ, and e. שלא הֶחֱזִיקוּ בשכר וכ׳ they did not cling to the duty of maintaining teachers &c.

—5) (see חֲזָקָה) to presume, to be under a certain impression, to be convinced. Yerushalmi Kiddushin IV, 66ᵇ היו מַחֲזִיקִין בו שהוא בנו וכ׳ if people were under the impression that a certain person was their neighbor’s son, but in his dying hour he declared &c. Ib. היו מ׳ אותו שהוא וכ׳ if people took him to be a relation of his; and e.—Chagigah 19ᵃ, see infra.

    Hof. - הוּחֲזָק (denominative of חֲזָקָה) to be presumed, be held for, be known for. Gittin 14ᵃ בשה׳ כפרן when the man is known to be a liar. Shevuot 34ᵇ, and from ה׳ כפרן (in such a case) he is considered a confirmed liar.—Yerushalmi Kiddushin l. common gender. bottom of page הוּחְזְקוּ if they were generally assumed (to be husband and wife); and from—Chagigah 19ᵃ הטובל לחולין וה׳ לחולין if one takes an immersion for the purpose of being enabled to partake of ordinary food and is considered (by himself) to have immersed for that purpose. Ib. טבל ולא ה׳ if he did immerse but did not have a certain purpose in view. Ib. עודיהו … ה׳ לדבר קל מחזיק עצמו וכ׳ as long as he has one foot yet in the water, when he had had in view a minor purpose for his bath, he may still change it for a higher purpose. Ib. אם לא ה׳ מחזיק if he had had no particular object in view, he may on coming out define the object for which he has bathed.—Part. מוּחֲזָק
1) held in possession, adhered to. Bekhoroth VIII, 9 ולא בראוי כבמ׳ nor does he take a double share of what is coming due to the estate as he does of what is held in possession; Bava Batra 55ᵃ; and from—Shabbat 130ᵃ עדיין היא מוּחֲזֶקֶת בידם it is still strongly adhered to, opposed מרופה, see רָפָה.

—2) being known, approved. Sifra K’dosh. Parah 3, Chaldaic V במ׳ לך when he is known to thee (to be a proselyte); and e.

—3) being sure, convinced, knowing from experience. Ketubot 25ᵇ מוּחֲזַקְנִי בזה וכ׳ (= מ׳ אני) I know this man to be a priest; and e.—Sifré Bamidbar 1, see supra.

    Hithpaël - הִתְחַזֵּק,

    Nithpaël - נִתְחַזֵּק
1) to become solid, strong. Yalkut Breishit 5 יִתְחַזֵּק, see preceding

—2) to feel encouraged, take courage. Berakhot 32ᵃ נ׳ בתפלה became emboldened to pray.

sections.en: One who puts the jar away in order that it shall not be broken, or if he inverted it in order to dry it, [If he did one of these things] so that he might draw more water with it, [the water he had already drawn] is valid; But if he intended to carry in it the ashes, it is invalid. One who cleared potsherds from a trough: If in order that it may hold more water, the water is valid; But if he intended that they should not hinder him when he pours out the water, it is invalid.
sections.he: הַמַּצְנִיעַ אֶת הֶחָבִית שֶׁלֹּא תִשָּׁבֵר, אוֹ שֶׁכְּפָאָהּ עַל פִּיהָ עַל מְנָת לְנַגְּבָהּ לְמַלֹּאת בָּהּ, כָּשֵׁר. לְהוֹלִיךְ בָּהּ אֶת הַקִּדּוּשׁ, פָּסוּל. הַמְפַנֶּה חֲרָסִין מִתּוֹךְ הַשֹּׁקֶת בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתַּחֲזִיק מַיִם הַרְבֵּה, כְּשֵׁרִין. וְאִם בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ מְעַכְּבִין אוֹתוֹ בְשָׁעָה שֶׁהוּא זוֹלֵף אֶת הַמַּיִם, פָּסוּל:

sections.en: One was carrying his water on his shoulder and he ruled in a matter of law, or showed others the way, or killed a snake or a scorpion, or picked up food in order to store it, it [the water] is invalid; But [if he picked up] food to eat, it is valid. [And if he killed] a snake or a scorpion that hindered him, it remains valid. Rabbi Judah said: this is the general rule: If the act was is in the nature of work, the mixture is invalid whether the man stopped or not, If it was not in the nature of work: If he stopped, it is invalid; But if he did not stop it remains valid.
sections.he: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ מֵימָיו עַל כְּתֵפוֹ וְהוֹרָה הוֹרָאָה, וְהֶרְאָה לַאֲחֵרִים אֶת הַדֶּרֶךְ, וְהָרַג נָחָשׁ וְעַקְרָב, וְנָטַל אֳכָלִים לְהַצְנִיעָם, פָּסוּל. אֳכָלִין לְאָכְלָן, כָּשֵׁר. הַנָּחָשׁ וְהָעַקְרָב שֶׁהָיוּ מְעַכְּבִים אוֹתוֹ, כָּשֵׁר. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוּם מְלָאכָה, בֵּין עָמַד בֵּין לֹא עָמַד, פָּסוּל. דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִשּׁוּם מְלָאכָה, עָמַד, פָּסוּל. וְאִם לֹא עָמַד, כָּשֵׁר:

sections.en: If one gave over his water to someone who was unclean, it is invalid. But if to a clean one it is valid. Rabbi Eliezer says: even if it was entrusted to an unclean man it is valid, provided the owner did no other work in the meantime.
sections.he: הַמּוֹסֵר מֵימָיו לְטָמֵא, פְּסוּלִין. וּלְטָהוֹר, כְּשֵׁרִין. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַף לְטָמֵא כְּשֵׁרִין, אִם לֹא עָשׂוּ הַבְּעָלִים מְלָאכָה:

sections.en: Two men who were drawing water for the hatat and one assisted the other to raise it or one pulled out a thorn for the other: For one mixture, it is valid; For two mixtures, it is invalid. Rabbi Yose says: even if there are to be two mixtures it is valid if they had made a mutual agreement between them.
sections.he: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁהָיוּ מְמַלְּאִין לְחַטָּאת, וְהִגְבִּיהוּ זֶה עַל זֶה וְנָטַל זֶה לָזֶה קוֹצוֹ, בְּקִדּוּשׁ אֶחָד, כָּשֵׁר. בִּשְׁנֵי קִדּוּשִׁין, פָּסוּל. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף בִּשְׁנֵי קִדּוּשִׁין כָּשֵׁר, אִם הִתְנוּ בֵינֵיהֶן:

sections.en: One who broke down a fence [even] with the intention of putting it up again, the water remains valid; But if he put a fence up, the water becomes invalid. If he ate figs intending to store some of them, the water is valid; But if he stored figs it is invalid. If he was eating figs and, leaving some over, threw what was in his hand under the fig tree or among drying figs in order that it shall not be wasted, the water is invalid.
sections.he: הַפּוֹרֵץ עַל מְנָת לִגְדֹּר, כָּשֵׁר. וְאִם גָּדַר, פָּסוּל. הָאוֹכֵל עַל מְנָת לִקְצוֹת, כָּשֵׁר. וְאִם קָצָה, פָּסוּל. הָיָה אוֹכֵל וְהוֹתִיר וְזָרַק מַה שֶּׁבְּיָדוֹ לְתַחַת הַתְּאֵנָה אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַמֻּקְצֶה בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא יֹאבַד, פָּסוּל:
